scenarios.title: TCP established but TLS did not complete normally

corroborating_orphan_candidates.Name: EndpointProtectionService
Reasons: Synthetic complete uninstall inventory does not list the expected application.

corroborating_orphan_candidates.Name: BdNet

corroborating_orphan_candidates.Name: Synthetic Endpoint Security
Reasons: Synthetic provider is registered while its main product file is missing.

scenarios.reasoning: Each recorded attempt completed TCP on the same socket before its TLS-stage failure. Relevant orphan evidence increases investigation priority when the differential repeats.
alternatives: TLS inspection or other intermediate equipment.
Certificate/time/trust-store failure when certificate validation is the measured error.
verification: Repeat identical targets and parameters; preserve all IPs and attempt outcomes.
Inspect read-only WFP/NDIS ownership evidence and compare before/after snapshots.
Use a trusted vendor removal procedure only after verifying product identity and suitability.
conditions: tcp_ms is present for each TLS-stage failure.
E3 requires repeated multi-target failures and independently enumerated relevant orphan candidates.
Correlation does not establish a kernel deadlock or identify a culpable driver.
scenarios.grade_definition: Corroborated: repeated differential measurements plus independent relevant configuration evidence; causality remains unproven.
scenarios.repair: No automatic system change is authorized by this hypothesis.

scenarios.title: Security or VPN component ownership needs review

evidence.Name: EndpointProtectionService
Reasons: Synthetic complete uninstall inventory does not list the expected application.

evidence.Name: BdNet
Reasons: Synthetic runtime driver enumeration remains after its service registration is absent.

evidence.Name: Synthetic Endpoint Security
Reasons: Synthetic provider is registered while its main product file is missing.

scenarios.reasoning: Independent inventory records show an ownership/registration inconsistency. Missing uninstall registration alone is not proof that the main program was removed.
alternatives: A shared SDK owned by a different installed product.
A component pending reboot or a stale security-center registration.
verification: Verify publisher signature, product metadata, service path and the current antivirus provider.
Compare the component with the installed-app list and a known-good snapshot.
conditions: The inventory completeness attached to the evidence supports the stated absence.
Names alone do not establish product ownership, malware or fault.
scenarios.grade_definition: Observed: a directly measured state or one failed attempt; cause is unconfirmed.
scenarios.repair: No automatic system change is authorized by this hypothesis.
